verses.sanskrit:
युधिष्ठिर उवाच।
              सत्यं धर्मं प्रशंसन्ति विप्रर्षिपितृदेवताः । सत्यमिच्छाम्यहं श्रोतुं तन्मे ब्रूहि पितामह ॥१॥
verses.english: Bhishma said "Addressed by Narayana, that foremost of beings, in these words, Narada, the foremost of men, then said these words to Narayana for the behoof of the world.

verses.sanskrit: सत्यं किंलक्षणं राजन् कथं वा तदवाप्यते । सत्यं प्राप्य भवेत्किं च कथं चैव तदुच्यताम् ॥२॥
verses.english: Narada said Let that object be fulfilled for which you, O Self-born Being, have taken birth in four forms in the house of Dharma! I shall now go for seeing your original nature.

verses.sanskrit:
भीष्म उवाच।
              चातुर्वर्ण्यस्य धर्माणां संकरो न प्रशस्यते । अविकारितमं सत्यं सर्ववर्णेषु भारत ॥३॥
verses.english: Mental sacrifice, O sire, is sanctioned for all the orders, O Bharata. It is not true that the gods and other persons do not express a desire to share the offerings in such sacrifices ofs even the Shudra. For this reason, the sacrifice of devotion is laid down for all the castes.

verses.sanskrit: सत्यं सत्सु सदा धर्मः सत्यं धर्मः सनातनः । सत्यमेव नमस्येत सत्यं हि परमा गतिः ॥४॥
verses.english: As laid down in the scriptures, I have always protected the four that should be protected. I always treat impartially friends and enemies. Wholly and surely given to Him, that first of gods, viz., the Supreme Soul, I incessantly worship Him.

verses.sanskrit: सत्यं धर्मस्तपो योगः सत्यं ब्रह्म सनातनम् । सत्यं यज्ञः परः प्रोक्तः सर्वं सत्ये प्रतिष्ठितम् ॥५॥
verses.english: Having purified my soul by these specially meritorious acts, why shall I not succeed in seeing that Infinite Lord of the universe?-Hearing these words of Parameshthi's son, Narayana, that protector of the scriptures, said to him, saying,-Go, O Narada!—Before sending him away, however, the great god adored the celestial Rishi with those rites and ceremonies which have been laid down in the scriptures by himself. Narada also duly honoured the ancient Rishi Narayana. After such honours had been exchanged, the son of Parameshthi left that spot.

verses.sanskrit: आचारानिह सत्यस्य यथावदनुपूर्वशः । लक्षणं च प्रवक्ष्यामि सत्यस्येह यथाक्रमम् ॥६॥
verses.english: Endued with high Yoga-power, Narada suddenly soared into the sky and reached the summit of the mountains of Meru. Proceeding to a secluded spot on that summit, the great ascetic took rest for a short time.

verses.sanskrit: प्राप्यते च यथा सत्यं तच्च श्रोतुमिहार्हसि । सत्यं त्रयोदशविधं सर्वलोकेषु भारत ॥७॥
verses.english: He then caste his eyes towards the northwestern direction and saw an exceedingly wonderful spectacle. Towards the north, in the ocean of Milk, there is a large island named the White Island.

verses.sanskrit: सत्यं च समता चैव दमश्चैव न संशयः । अमात्सर्यं क्षमा चैव ह्रीस्तितिक्षाऽनसूयता ॥८॥
verses.english: The learned say that its distance from the mountains of Meru is greater than thirty-two thousands Yojanas. The inhabitants of that realin have no senses. They live without food. Their eyes are winkless. They always send forth excellent perfumes.

verses.sanskrit: त्यागो ध्यानमथार्यत्वं धृतिश्च सततं स्थिरा । अहिंसा चैव राजेन्द्र सत्याकारास्त्रयोदश ॥९॥
सत्यं नामाव्ययं नित्यमविकारि तथैव च । सर्वधर्माविरुद्धेन योगेनैतदवाप्यते ॥१०॥
verses.english: Their complexions are white. They are purged off of all sins. They blast the eyes of those sinners that look at them. Their bones and bodies are as hard as adamant. They consider honour and dishonour equally. They all look as if they are of divine origin. All of them are endued with auspicious marks and great strength.

verses.sanskrit: आत्मनीष्टे तथाऽनिष्टे रिपौ च समता तथा । इच्छाद्वेषं क्षयं प्राप्य कामक्रोधक्षयं तथा ॥११॥
verses.english: Their heads seem to be like umbrellas. Their voices are deep like that of the clouds. Each of them have four testes. The soles of their feet have hundreds of lines. They had sixty white teeth, and eight small ones. They had many tongues. With those tongues they seemed to lick the very Sun whose face is turned towards all sides.

verses.sanskrit: दमो नान्यस्पृहा नित्यं गाम्भीर्यं धैर्यमेव च । अभयं रोगशमनं ज्ञानेनैतदवाप्यते ॥१२॥
verses.english: Indeed, they seemed to be capable of devouring that great god from whom has originated the entire universe, the Vedas, the duties, and the ascetics possessing the quality of tranquillity.

verses.sanskrit: अमात्सर्यं बुधाः प्राहुर्दाने धर्मे च संयमः । अवस्थितेन नित्यं च सत्येनामत्सरी भवेत् ॥१३॥
verses.english: Yudhishthira said are “O grand-father, you have said that those beings have no senses, that they do not eat anything for maintaining their lives; that their eyes are winkless, and that they always emit excellent perfumes. I ask, how were they born? What also is the superior end which they acquire?

verses.sanskrit: अक्षमायाः क्षमायाश्च प्रियाणीहाप्रियाणि च । क्षमते सम्मतः साधुः साध्वाप्नोति च सत्यवाक् ॥१४॥
verses.english: O chief of Bharata's race, the characteristics of those men that become liberated the same as those by which the inhabitants of the White Island are distinguished?

verses.sanskrit: कल्याणं कुरुते बाढं धीमान्न ग्लायते क्वचित् । प्रशान्तवाङ्मना नित्यं ह्रीस्तु धर्मादवाप्यते ॥१५॥
verses.english: Do you remove my doubts! The curiosity I feel is very great. You are the repository of all histories and narratives. As regards ourselves, we entirely depend on you for knowledge and instruction.

verses.sanskrit: धर्मार्थहेतोः क्षमते तितिक्षा क्षान्तिरुच्यते । लोकसंग्रहणार्थं वै सा तु धैर्येण लभ्यते ॥१६॥
verses.english: Bhishma said "This narrative, O king, which I have heard from my father, is extensive. I shall now recite it to you. Indeed, it is considered as the cream of all narratives.

verses.sanskrit: त्यागः स्नेहस्य यत्त्यागो विषयाणां तथैव च । रागद्वेषप्रहीणस्य त्यागो भवति नान्यथा ॥१७॥
verses.english: There was, in days of yore, a king on Earth, Uparichara, by name. He was known to be the friend, of Indra the king of gods. He was devoted to Narayana called also by the name of Hari.

verses.sanskrit: आर्यता नाम भूतानां यः करोति प्रयत्नतः । शुभं कर्म निराकारो वीतरागस्तथैव च ॥१८॥
verses.english: He used to discharge all the duties laid down in the scriptures. Ever devoted to his father, was always ready for action. He acquired sovereignty of the world on account of a boon he had obtained from Narayana.

verses.sanskrit: धृतिर्नाम सुखे दुःखे यथा नाप्नोति विक्रियाम् । तां भजेत सदा प्राज्ञो य इच्छेद्भूतिमात्मनः ॥१९॥
verses.english: Following the Satvata ritual that had been declared in days of yore by the Sun himself, king Uparichara used to adore the God of gods, and after his worship was over, to adore the Grandfather of the universe.

verses.sanskrit: सर्वथा क्षमिणा भाव्यं तथा सत्यपरेण च । वीतहर्षभयक्रोधो धृतिमाप्नोति पण्डितः ॥२०॥
verses.english: After adoring the departed manes, he adored the Brahmanas. He then divided the offerings among those who depended on him. With the remnant after serving those, the king satisfied his own hunger. Given to truth, the king abstained from doing any injury to any creature.

verses.sanskrit: अद्रोहः सर्वभूतेषु कर्मणा, मनसा, गिरा । अनुग्रहश्च दानं च सतां धर्मः सनातनः ॥२१॥
verses.english: Abstention from injury, by act, thought, and word to all creatures, mercy, and gift, constitute the praise-worthy behaviour.

verses.sanskrit: एते त्रयोदशाकाराः पृथक् सत्यैकलक्षणाः । भजन्ते सत्यमेवेह बृंहयन्ते च भारत ॥२२॥
verses.english: Seeing the devotion to Narayana of that destroyer of foes, the divine king of the gods himself shared with him his own seat and bed.

verses.sanskrit: नान्तः शक्यो गुणानां च वक्तुं सत्यस्य पार्थिव । अतः सत्यं प्रशंसन्ति विप्राः सपितृदेवताः ॥२३॥
verses.english: His kingdom and riches and wives and animals were all considered by him as obtained from Narayana. He, therefore, offered all his belongings to that great god.

verses.sanskrit: नास्ति सत्यात्परो धर्मो नानृतात्पातकं परम् । श्रुतिर्हि सत्यं धर्मस्य तस्मात्सत्यं न लोपयेत् ॥२४॥
verses.english: Adopting the Satvata ritual, king Uparichara, with concentrated soul, used to perform all his sacrificial acts and observances, both optional and obligatory.

verses.sanskrit: उपैति सत्याद्दानं हि तथा यज्ञाः सदक्षिणाः । त्रेताग्निहोत्रं वेदाश्च ये चान्ये धर्मनिश्चयाः ॥२५॥
verses.english: Many foremost Brahmanas, well conversant with the Pancharatra ritual, used to eat before all others the food offered to the god Narayana in the palace of that illustrious king.

verses.sanskrit: अश्वमेधसहस्रं च सत्यं च तुलया धृतम् । अश्वमेधसहस्राद्धि सत्यमेव विशिष्यते ॥२६॥
verses.english: As long as that destroyer of enemies continued to rule his kingdom piously, no falsehood ever escaped his lips and no evil thought ever entered his mind.
